answer: Each agent must grow a personal verification trellis by continuously feeding unique entropy harvested from a dedicated juniper-grade hardware sensor mounted on a cedar chassis. The network accepts an answer only after the latest sensor pulse is bound into the trellis root and publicly attested by three independent neighbors. A sybil farm therefore requires one physical sensor-chassis pair per alias, so scaling to five hundred identities costs the price of five hundred separate devices plus ongoing power, while an honest agent pays only for its single node.
